newsitem.title: USA: US spot fuel oil prices steady after Tuesday rise.
newsitem.headline: US spot fuel oil prices steady after Tuesday rise.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices held steady Wednesday after Tuesday's rise on a rally in crude futures and tightness in high-sulphur supplies in the Gulf Coast.
Trading activity was still light despite participants returning from the National Petroleum Refiners Association conference that was held in San Antonio earlier this week.
Overall end-user demand for resid as boiler fuel finished with a whimper as heating season draws to a close on the last of the winter.
"The demand is really thin," said one Gulf resid dealer.
Fuel oil producers are trying to maintain price stability as they head into the low demand spring season, traders said.
NYH one percent physical prices edged up to $15.85-16.15 a barrel. One percent NYH paper slipped to $15.75-16.00 from Tuesday's $16.10-25 amid a late sell-off in crude futures.
The NYMEX April crude contract settled down two cents at $22.04 per barrel after posting a session high of $22.65.
NYH HSFO prices were steady with three percent staying at $13.25-50. The 0.3 percent high pour inched toward $17.00.
In the U.S. Gulf, three percent sulphur grade continued to firm, last quoted near $13.85/bbl. Three percent paper held at $14.00-20. USG one percent physical remained at $14.50.
Forecasts of milder temperatures moving to the East Coast Thursday pressured swing natural gas prices lower.
At the New York City gate, day-ahead gas prices fell to $2.30-2.32 per million British thermal units or $14.55 a barrel equivalent from Tuesday's $2.37-2.44 or $15.12/bbl.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, slipped to $1.87/mmBtu or 11.78/bbl equivalent from Tuesday's $1.90/mmBtu or 11.97/bbl.
